title: COP31 Climate Summit Ends Without Final Agreement
subtitle: Global leaders fail to reach a consensus as divisions over fossil fuels and funding stall progress.

summary.en: The COP31 climate summit in Turkey has officially ended without a final agreement. This is the first time since 2009 that countries failed to reach a consensus on a concluding statement. Major disagreements centered on the future of fossil fuels and financial support for developing nations. Despite the lack of an overall deal, some smaller programs were approved. The failure highlights deep global divisions regarding how to address the climate crisis.
summary.zh: 在土耳其舉行的第 31 屆聯合國氣候變遷大會已正式落幕，但未能達成最終協議。這是自 2009 年以來，各國首次未能就總結聲明達成共識。主要爭議集中在化石燃料的未來以及對開發中國家的財務支持。儘管缺乏整體協議，會議仍批准了一些較小規模的計畫。此次失敗凸顯了全球在如何應對氣候危機方面的深刻分歧。

paragraphs.en: The COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, has officially come to an end without a final agreement. For the first time since 2009, the conference concluded without a "cover decision." This is a concluding statement that usually shows the world is united on how to fight the worsening climate crisis. The event, which lasted longer than any previous climate conference in history, left many participants feeling that the goals of the meeting were not met.
paragraphs.zh: 在土耳其安塔利亞（Antalya）舉行的第 31 屆聯合國氣候變遷大會（COP31）已正式落幕，但未能達成最終協議。這是自 2009 年以來，該會議首次未能產出「總結決議」。這份總結聲明通常用以展現全球在應對日益嚴峻的氣候危機上團結一致。此次會議的舉辦時間比歷史上任何一場氣候會議都長，許多與會者感到會議目標並未達成。

paragraphs.en: According to Ars Technica, the conference center felt like a place where hopes had been broken. Murat Kurum, the president of the conference and Turkey’s minister of environment, urbanization, and climate change, tried to bring countries together to sign a final deal. However, many nations refused to support the proposal. The European Union, along with several Latin American countries and Pacific Island states, stated they would not accept the text as it was written.
paragraphs.zh: 根據科技媒體 Ars Technica 報導，會議中心瀰漫著希望破滅的氣氛。大會主席兼土耳其環境、都市化與氣候變遷部長庫魯姆（Murat Kurum）試圖促成各國簽署最終協議，然而許多國家拒絕支持該提案。歐盟（European Union）以及多個拉丁美洲國家與太平洋島國表示，無法接受該草案的內容。

paragraphs.en: This failure to agree was caused by deep divisions between nations. One major point of disagreement was whether the final document should mention fossil fuels—such as oil, gas, and coal—and carbon capture technology. Carbon capture is a process that traps carbon dioxide emissions before they enter the atmosphere. Some countries wanted a strong commitment to move away from these energy sources, while others were hesitant to agree to such language.
paragraphs.zh: 未能達成共識的原因在於各國之間存在深刻分歧。爭議焦點之一在於最終文件是否應提及石油、天然氣與煤炭等化石燃料，以及碳捕捉技術。碳捕捉是一種在二氧化碳排放進入大氣層前將其攔截的技術。部分國家希望明確承諾擺脫這些能源，但其他國家對於採用此類措辭感到猶豫。

paragraphs.en: Another major issue was climate financing. This refers to money provided by wealthy, developed nations to help poorer, developing countries deal with the effects of climate change. Many developing nations are already suffering from costly climate disasters and feel that they need more financial support to adapt to these changes. The goal of the summit was to increase this funding, but countries could not agree on how much should be provided.
paragraphs.zh: 另一個主要議題是氣候融資。這指的是由富裕的已開發國家提供資金，協助較貧窮的開發中國家應對氣候變遷的影響。許多開發中國家已深受氣候災難帶來的沉重代價所苦，認為需要更多財務支持以適應這些變化。本次峰會的目標原為增加此類資金，但各國無法就資助金額達成共識。

paragraphs.en: Despite the lack of a final, overarching agreement, the conference did manage to pass some smaller decisions. For example, countries approved a program to help workers and communities transition away from fossil fuels. They also created a plan to better track progress on climate adaptation, which means making changes to protect people and nature from the impacts of a warming planet. These smaller steps were seen as positive, but they did not make up for the failure to reach a larger, global deal.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管缺乏最終的總體協議，會議仍通過了一些較小規模的決議。例如，各國批准了一項協助勞工與社區從化石燃料轉型的計畫。他們也制定了一項計畫，以更有效地追蹤氣候適應的進展，即採取措施保護人類與自然免受地球暖化的影響。這些小步進展被視為正面成果，但仍無法彌補未能達成更大規模全球協議的遺憾。

paragraphs.en: To understand why this matters, it is helpful to look at the history of these meetings. In 2022, the UN conference in Egypt agreed to create a "loss and damage" fund. This fund is designed to help vulnerable countries pay for climate impacts that are already happening and cannot be reversed. A year later, in Dubai, delegates from more than 190 countries agreed for the first time that the world needs a "just and orderly" transition away from fossil fuels. This meant moving to cleaner energy in a way that is fair to all workers and economies.
paragraphs.zh: 若要理解為何此事至關重要，回顧這些會議的歷史很有幫助。2022 年，聯合國在埃及舉行的會議同意設立「損失與損害」基金。該基金旨在協助脆弱國家支付已發生且無法逆轉的氣候影響所造成的損失。一年後，在杜拜，來自 190 多個國家的代表首次同意全球需要「公正且有序地」擺脫化石燃料。這意味著在轉向潔淨能源的過程中，必須對所有勞工與經濟體保持公平。

paragraphs.en: Going into this summit, the goal was to build on those past successes. Leaders wanted to set clear, voluntary goals for the widespread use of electricity across global economies. They also hoped to strengthen international efforts to slow down global warming. However, the final days of the summit were marked by intense arguments. Reports from the event noted that the talks continued well past their scheduled end date as nations fought over the specific wording regarding fossil fuels.
paragraphs.zh: 本次峰會召開前，目標是延續過去的成功經驗。各國領袖希望為全球經濟廣泛使用電力設定明確的自願性目標，並期望加強國際合作以減緩全球暖化。然而，峰會最後幾天充滿了激烈的爭論。據報導，由於各國針對化石燃料的具體措辭爭執不下，談判時間遠超預定結束日期。

paragraphs.en: Moving forward, the failure to reach a consensus at COP31 raises questions about the future of global climate cooperation. When countries cannot agree on a final statement, it becomes harder to show that the world is moving in the same direction. As cleaning crews removed the debris from the conference center, the mood remained uncertain. While the world continues to face the reality of a changing climate, the path toward a unified global solution remains difficult and full of challenges. The international community will now have to decide how to bridge these deep gaps before the next meeting.
paragraphs.zh: 展望未來，COP31 未能達成共識引發了對全球氣候合作前景的質疑。當各國無法就最終聲明達成一致時，要展現全球正朝同一方向邁進就變得更加困難。當清潔人員清理會議中心的廢棄物時，氣氛依然充滿不確定性。儘管全球持續面臨氣候變遷的現實，邁向統一全球解決方案的道路依然艱難且充滿挑戰。國際社會現在必須決定如何在下次會議前彌合這些巨大的分歧。

keyTerms.definitionEn: Serving as a primary or comprehensive summary statement for a formal agreement.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 作為總結性、涵蓋性的（決議）。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作動詞（覆蓋），這裡用作形容詞修飾 decision，指代會議的總結性文件。文中：For the first time since 2009, the conference concluded without a "cover decision."

keyTerms.definitionEn: To compensate for something bad with something good.
keyTerms.noteZh: 由動詞與介系詞組成，意思與字面拆開看不同。文中：These smaller steps were seen as positive, but they did not make up for the failure to reach a larger, global deal.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To reduce the differences between two things or groups.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（橋樑），這裡作動詞，形容處理國家間的嚴重分歧。文中：The international community will now have to decide how to bridge these deep gaps before the next meeting.

quiz.question: What specific outcome regarding the final text of the COP31 conference makes it unique compared to climate summits since 2009?

options.A: It was the first conference to focus exclusively on carbon capture technology.
options.B: It was the first summit in that timeframe to conclude without a 'cover decision'.
options.C: It was the first time in history that the conference ended before its scheduled date.
options.D: It was the first time that no developing nations attended the final negotiations.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據第一段，文章明確指出這是自 2009 年以來，首次沒有達成「總結決議」（cover decision）的氣候峰會。選項 A 錯誤，因為文章僅提到碳捕捉是爭議點之一，並非會議唯一主題。選項 C 與文章第一段描述的「持續時間比歷史上任何會議都長」完全相反。選項 D 在文中並未提及，且事實上發展中國家積極參與了關於氣候融資的討論。

quiz.question: Based on the text, why did the European Union and several other nations reject the proposed final text?

options.A: They felt the document did not provide enough funding for their own domestic climate projects.
options.B: They disagreed with the specific language used regarding fossil fuels and carbon capture.
options.C: They wanted to postpone the conference until the following year to allow more time for research.
options.D: They believed that the conference center in Antalya was not suitable for such a large event.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。綜合文章第二段與第三段，第二段提到歐盟與其他國家拒絕該文本，而第三段緊接著說明「分歧的主要點」在於最終文件是否應提及化石燃料與碳捕捉技術，由此可推論這正是他們拒絕的原因。選項 A 錯誤，因為氣候融資主要涉及已開發國家對開發中國家的援助。選項 C 與 D 在文中皆無相關證據支持，屬於無中生有的干擾選項。

quiz.question: In the final paragraph, what does the word 'bridge' mean in the context of 'bridge these deep gaps'?

options.A: To build a physical construction over a river or obstacle.
options.B: To ignore or forget about existing disagreements.
options.C: To find a way to reduce differences and reach an agreement.
options.D: To increase the distance between opposing political parties.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。在此語境下，「bridge gaps」是一種比喻用法，意指「彌合分歧」或「縮小差距」，即透過協商達成共識。選項 A 是該詞的字面意義，在此處不適用。選項 B 錯誤，因為文章強調國際社會必須解決這些分歧，而非無視它們。選項 D 的意思與「bridge」完全相反，因為彌合分歧是為了讓雙方更靠近，而非拉大距離。

quiz.question: What is the central message of the article regarding the COP31 climate summit?

options.A: The summit was a complete success because it established a new program for workers.
options.B: The summit proved that global cooperation on climate change is no longer necessary.
options.C: The summit highlighted the ongoing difficulties in reaching a unified global agreement on climate action.
options.D: The summit focused primarily on the technical aspects of carbon capture rather than political issues.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章從頭到尾都在討論 COP31 無法達成最終協議的困境，並在結尾提到這引發了對未來全球氣候合作的質疑，強調了達成統一解決方案的困難。選項 A 過於片面，文章雖提到有小進展，但明確表示這些無法彌補未能達成大協議的失敗。選項 B 與文章主旨背道而馳，文章強調的是合作的必要性與挑戰。選項 D 錯誤，因為政治上的分歧（如融資與化石燃料政策）才是會議失敗的主因。
